primitives.name: Contest Trajectory Factor
primitives.verbatim_quote: 2014), little has been done to study why contesting shots decreases field-goal percentage (FG%) and how contests affect the trajectory of shots.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'NDD': 'nearest defender distance (feet)', 'depth': 'shot depth relative to rim (feet)', 'angle': 'entry angle to rim (degrees)', 'deviation': 'left-right deviation from center (inches)'}
primitives.assumptions: Shot trajectories follow deterministic paths under constant gravity; defender influence modeled as linear perturbation in spatial dimensions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When NDD < 4 feet, shot factor variance increases exponentially due to reduced reaction time.

layer2.mapping: Kernel-based regression maps NDD to expected shot factor changes using empirical shot trajectory data.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error between predicted and actual shot factor deviations.

primitives.name: Defensive Impact Probability
primitives.verbatim_quote: Utilizing shot trajectories and corresponding modeled shot-make probabilities, we are able to create perimeter defensive metrics that are more accurate and less variable than traditional metrics like opponent field goal percentage.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathbb{P}(\\text{make})': 'probability of making shot', '\\beta_i': 'regression coefficient (dimensionless)', 'depth': 'shot depth (feet)', 'angle': 'entry angle (degrees)', 'deviation': 'lateral deviation (inches)'}
primitives.assumptions: Conditional independence of shot factors; logistic link function models probability of make.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When shot factors exceed thresholds (depth > 2 ft, angle < 30°), model becomes unreliable due to sparse data.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to Bayesian belief update over shot outcomes conditioned on defensive contest parameters.
layer2.telemetry: Brier score of predicted vs observed shot outcomes.

primitives.name: Perimeter Defense Metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: Metrics like opponent FG% and perimeter defense rating that try to quantify perimeter defense still rely on counting discrete events and can be highly variable.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\text{PDM}': 'perimeter defense metric (dimensionless)', '\\mathbb{P}(\\text{miss}_i)': 'probability of miss for shot i', 'n': 'number of contested shots'}
primitives.assumptions: Each shot contributes independently to PDM; contest is binary (tight or not tight).
primitives.breakdown_regime: When n < 100, metric exhibits high variance due to insufficient samples.

layer2.mapping: Kernel smoothing applied to PDM over time windows to reduce noise and improve stability.
layer2.telemetry: Standard deviation of rolling PDM over 10-game windows.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that shot trajectories encode latent defensive impact through measurable geometric properties—depth, angle, and lateral deviation. These are modeled using Bayesian hierarchical regression to estimate how tightly contested shots deviate from optimal paths. The contest trajectory factor primitive formalizes this by treating defender proximity as a perturbative force on shot geometry. The defensive impact probability primitive leverages this to compute per-shot make probabilities conditioned on trajectory features. Finally, the perimeter defense metric aggregates these probabilities into a scalar descriptor of defensive performance. Each primitive operates under the assumption of deterministic shot dynamics modulated by stochastic defensive interference. Failure modes arise when shot data is sparse or when defenders are too distant to meaningfully alter trajectory, leading to ill-conditioned regressions or noisy estimates.
